NET-NEW: PortalListingsRepository.getPortfolioAnalytics() (realtor portfolio analytics screen) performs an UNBOUNDED concurrent fan-out - not touched by any prior slice. listMyListings(limit = 100) then one async getListingAnalytics() per listing, awaitAll, no Semaphore/chunk cap => up to 100 simultaneous HTTP requests through the single shared Ktor client. Compounds the already-filed missing-HttpTimeout: a stalled analytics endpoint stalls up to 100 coroutines at once for a power-realtor.

ViewModel concurrency sweep (ListingDetailViewModel, PriceTrackingViewModel): NO finding. scope is a lifecycle-bound rememberCoroutineScope (cancelled on leave-composition); favorite/inquiry writes are session-pinned and documented; retry()->loadListing() sets isLoading=true which flips the UI state-machine off the error/retry branch, so the double-tap race is not reachable. Concurrency is carefully handled - consistent with the prior reviewer's judgment.

Network error-handling re-check on PortalListingsRepository: listMyListings/getListingAnalytics both wrap in try/catch -> Result.failure; getPortfolioAnalytics + toggleSearchAlert are not wrapped but only delegate to already-wrapped Result-returning calls, so no exception escapes. No swallow/throw finding.

Repository test coverage is strong (commonTest has per-repo + path-encoding + contract tests incl. getPortfolioAnalytics fold/date-merge cases); but there is no test exercising the large-portfolio fan-out behaviour (concurrency bound). Noted as part of the net-new finding rather than a separate test-gap row.

evidence: mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/realtor/PortalListingsRepository.kt:111-125 - getPortfolioAnalytics() calls listMyListings(limit = 100) then fans out one getListingAnalytics(listing.id) async per listing inside coroutineScope { listings.map { async { ... } }.awaitAll() } with NO concurrency cap (no Semaphore, no chunked().flatMap). A realtor with a large portfolio triggers up to 100 simultaneous HTTP requests through the single shared HttpClientProvider.client.

Impact: on the realtor ListingAnalytics portfolio screen this is a self-inflicted request storm - it can exhaust the Ktor client connection pool, trip server-side rate limits, and (because the shared client has no HttpTimeout plugin - see the already-filed code-review-mobile-native-kmp-http-client-no-timeout) leave up to 100 coroutines stalled at once on a slow analytics endpoint, with the whole portfolio view blocked on awaitAll.

Fix: bound the fan-out - a kotlinx.coroutines Semaphore(n) around each async, or listings.chunked(n).flatMap { it.map { async{} }.awaitAll() }, with a small n (e.g. 6-8); add a large-portfolio test asserting the concurrency cap. Net-new: not covered by the 2026-10-30 sibling slice nor any prior mobile-native-kmp review.
